verses.text: Incident of the debate between king Namrud and Ibraheem (a.s). Namrud argued with Ibraheem (a.s) about his Rabb. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 35)

Ibraheem (a.s) said, that Allah has the power to give life and to cause death. Namrud replied that he also has the same power (indicating that he could let free any prisoner who was to be executed and put to death any person whom he wished) (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 35)

Ibraheem (a.s) then said, “Allah causes the sun to rise from the east; just make it rise from the west”. Namrud could not argue any further. Surely, Allah does not guide the wrongdoers. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 35)

Incident of Ibraheem (a.s) is mentioned, when he asked Allah to show how He gives life to the dead. Allah asked: “Have you no faith in this?” And Ibraheem a.s replied that he asks this only to reassure his heart. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 35)

Allah then told Ibraheem a.s to train four birds who would come back when called. Then to cut them into pieces and scatter those pieces on hilltops. Allah then brought them back to life and they came flying back. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 35)

Reminder of the debate between Ibraheem (a.s) and the people who worshipped the stars. When night came, Ibraheem (a.s) pretended to worship a star. But when the star set, he said: “I do not like to worship that which fades away”. (Surah Al-An’am : Section 9)

The next day he pretended to worship the moon and when it set he declared that this cannot be my Rabb. Following day, when he saw the sun shining bright, he said, this must be my Rabb. But when it also set, he said: “O my people! I am free of your shirk. (Surah Al-An’am : Section 9)
Ibraheem a.s. finally concluded: “I have turned my face sincerely to Him Who has created the heavens and the earth, and I am not one of the polytheist.” (Surah Al-An’am : Section 9)
When the people started arguing with Ibraheem, he said “I do not fear those whom you have taken for gods besides Allah, none can harm me unless my Rabb so wills”. (Surah Al-An’am : Section 9)

Ibraheem (a.s) prayed for his father’s forgiveness only to fulfill a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear, that he was an enemy of Allah, Ibraheem (a.s) disassociated himself from his father. (Surah At-Tauba : Section 14)
The fact is that Ibraheem (a.s) was tender hearted, forbearing. (Surah At-Tauba : Section 14)
Relate to them (O Prophet s.a.w.s), the story of Ibraheem (a.s). He was a truthful Prophet. (Surah Maryam : Section 3)
He said to his father: “O my father! Why do you worship something that can neither hear nor see, nor profit you in any way?” (Surah Maryam : Section 3)
Ibraheem a.s continued: “O my father! I have been given some knowledge which has not come to you. So follow me: I shall guide you to the Right Way”. (Surah Maryam : Section 3)

He further continued: “O my father! Do not worship Shaitaan for he is disobedient to Allah. O my father! I fear that a punishment from Allah may afflict you and you may become a friend of Shaitaan”. (Surah Maryam : Section 3)
His father said to him – ‘How dare you renounce my gods O Ibraheem? Be gone, and if you do not stop this folly, I will stone you to death’. (Surah Maryam : Section 3)
Ibraheem a.s says to his father, “Peace be upon you, I will pray to my Rabb for your forgiveness. I am leaving you and all those deities whom you invoke, besides Allah”. (Surah Maryam : Section 3)

Allah granted to Ibraheem a.s descendants like Ishaaq and Yaqoob, and Allah made each of them a Prophet. Allah bestowed Mercy on them and granted them the honor of being mentioned with true high respect. (Surah Maryam : Section 3)
Allah blessed Ibraheem (a.s) with righteousness, and Allah knew him well. (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5)

Reminder of the incident when Ibraheem (a.s) asked his father and his people about the idols that they were devoted to. They replied: “We found our forefathers worshipping them”. (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5)
Ibraheem (a.s) said: “Then certainly both you and your forefathers have been in manifest error.” (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5)

He openly declared that it is Allah Who has created the heavens and the earth and is your Rabb. He further said that he will plan against the idols after the people have left (the temple). (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5)
So he broke all the idols to pieces, except the biggest of them. (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5)

When the people saw the plight of the idols, they said that it should be Ibraheem who did it. They called upon Ibraheem to question him and so that they can punish him severely. (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5)
Ibraheem (a.s) replied: “It is rather this chief of theirs (i.e the big idol) who has done it. Ask them, if they can speak!” (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5)

The people were in a state of confusion and said: “You know fully well that they cannot speak.” At this Ibraheem replied: “Do you then worship these deities instead of Allah? Shame on you and on those deities you worship besides Allah! Have you no sense at all?” (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5
The people had no answer but to say: “Burn him alive and avenge your gods”. (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5)
When they threw him into the massive fire, Allah commanded: “O fire! Be cool and comfortable for Ibraheem”. Thus Allah made them the big loosers. (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5)
Allah delivered Ibraheem (a.s) and his nephew Lut (a.s), and directed them to a land (i.e Syria), which Allah had blessed for all the people of the world. (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5)
Allah gave Ibraheem (a.s) a son, Ishaaq (Isaac) and then a grandson Yaqoob (Jacob). Allah made each of them a righteous man. (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 5)

Reminder of the story of Ibraheem (a.s) is given. He called upon his father and his people saying: “What is that which you worship?” To this they replied: “We worship idols, and sit beside them with all devotion”. (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 5)

Ibraheem (a.s) reasoned with them to worship one Allah, the Rabb of the Worlds. He said that these idols can neither hear you when you call on them, nor help you or harm you. The people said that they have found their forefathers worshipping these deities. (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 5)

Ibraheem (a.s) prayed: “O my Rabb! Bestow wisdom upon me and admit me among the righteous. Grant me a reputation of truthfulness on the tongue of later generations and count me among the inheritors of the paradise of Bliss”. (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 5)
Ibraheem (a.s) said to his people: “Worship Allah and fear Him; this is better for you if you understand”. (Surah Al-Ankabut : Section 2)
But the people (who were steeped in idol worship), had no answer except to say: “Kill him!” or “Burn him!”. (Surah AlAnkabut : Section 3)
But Allah (made the fire cool and comfortable for Ibraheem) and saved him. Surely, in this incident, there are signs for those who believe. (Surah Al-Ankabut : Section 3)

Ibraheem (a.s) addressed to the people: “Today you have made idols instead of Allah, a means of affection among yourselves in this worldly life, but, on the Day of Resurrection you shall disown and curse one another. Fire shall be your abode and you shall have no helper”. (Surah Al-Ankabut : Section 3)
(Witnessing the whole incident) Lut (a.s) believed in Ibraheem. (Surah Al-Ankabut : Section 3)
Finally, Ibraheem (a.s) said “I will migrate to where my Rabb will take me. Allah is the Mighty, the Wise”. (Surah Al-Ankabut : Section 3)

Reminder is made of the incident when Ibraheem (a.s) and Ismail (a.s) cleansed the Kabah and Ibraheem (a.s) prayed to Allah to make Makkah a secure town and provide its people with plenty of fruits and foods. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 15)

Ibraheem (a.s) and Ismail (a.s) raised the foundations of the Kabah and made a beautiful dua together- “Accept this from us, O Allah and make us both Muslims, (submissive to you), and also our descendants and show us ways of worship and accept our repentance. You are the Acceptor of repentance, the Merciful. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 15)

O our Rabb, appoint from among us a Rasool who shall recite Your Revelations and teach them the Book and the Wisdom, and purify them”. (The answer to this prayer is our beloved Prophet Muhammad s.a.w.s.). (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 15)
They argue if Ibraheem (a.s) was a Christian or Jew. You know that the Torah and Injeel were revealed long after Ibraheem a.s. Will you not then understand? (Surah Al-e-Imran : Section 7)
Ibraheem a.s was neither a Jew nor a Christian but he was a Muslim, true in faith. (Surah Al-e-Imran : Section 7)

Who has a better Deen (i.e. a way of life or religion), than the one who is a Muslim. Who submits himself entirely to Allah, is a doer of good and follows the faith of Ibraheem, the upright one; whom Allah chose to be His friend. (Surah An-Nisa : Section 18)

To Ibraheem (a.s), Allah gave descendants such as Ishaaq and Yaqoob, and Allah guided them like he guided Nuh. And among Ibraheem’s descendants were Daud, Sulaiman, Ayub, Yousuf, Musa, Haroon, Zakariya, Yahya, Isa, Illyas, Ismail, Al-Yas’a, Yunus and Lut (a.s). Allah exalted all of them over the worlds. (Surah Al-An’am : Section 10)
The angels visited Ibraheem (a.s) with good news. He offered a roasted calf to them, which they did not eat and Ibraheem (a.s) started to be afraid of them. (Surah Hud : Section 7)

News of a son (Ishaaq a.s), and after him a grandson (Yaqoob a.s) were given to Ibraheem. The wife of Ibraheem a.s expressed surprise and wonder at this news as she was an old woman. (Surah Hud : Section 7)

The angels said: “Do you wonder at Allah’s decree? May Allah’s mercy and His blessings be upon you O residents of this household; for Allah is indeed worthy of all praise, full of glory”. (Surah Hud : Section 7)

Ibraheem a.s made a dua and said: - “My Rabb! Make this city (Makkah) a city of peace, and save me and my sons from the worship of idols. Only those who follow my ways belong to me, and as for those who disobey me; surely You are Forgiving, Merciful”. (Surah Ibraheem : Section 6)

Referring to Ismail a.s, who was left to stay in the barren valley at Makkah, Ibraheem a.s prayed: “Turn the hearts of some people towards my offspring, whom I have settled near your Sacred House, and provide them with fruits, so they may give thanks”. (Surah Ibraheem : Section 6)

Ibraheem a.s continued: “O my Rabb, make me one who establishes Salaah and also from my descendants. Our Rabb! Accept my prayer. Our Rabb! Forgive me and my parents and all believers on the Day when the accountability will take place”. (Surah Ibraheem : Section 6)
Mention is made of the incident when Angels (in the form of messengers) visited Ibraheem a.s and gave him good news of a son, endowed with knowledge. (Surah Al-Hijr : Section 4)

Ibraheem (a.s) had gotten old and expressed surprise on the news, wherein the angels asked him not to despair. To this Ibraheem a.s replied: “Who would despair of the mercy of his Rabb, except those who are astray?”. (Surah Al-Hijr : Section 4)
Ibraheem (a.s) was an Ummah (an exemplary leader) an upright man, obedient to Allah. He was always grateful for the favors of Allah. (Surah An-Nahl : Section 16)
Allah gave him a good life in this world and in the hereafter he will be among the righteous. (Surah An-Nahl : Section 16)

Allah identified the site of the Sacred House to Ibraheem (a.s), saying: “Worship none besides Allah, keep the House of Allah pure for those who make Tawaf (i.e walking counterclockwise around the Ka’bah), stand in prayer, bow and prostrate themselves to Allah”. (Surah Al-Hajj : Section 4)
Allah further said: “O Ibraheem, make a proclamation of Hajj (Pilgrimage) to mankind: they will come to you on foot and on lean camels from every distant quarter. (Surah Al-Hajj : Section 4)

When Allah sent down angels (in the form of messengers) to Ibraheem (a.s) with good news (of the birth of a son) they said: “We are to destroy the people of that township, for its people are indeed wrongdoers”. (Surah Al-Ankabut : Section 4)

Ibraheem (a.s) pleaded: “But Lut is in there.” The angels replied: “We know who is in there: we shall certainly save him and his family, except his wife, who will remain behind.” (Surah Al-Ankabut : Section 4)

Reminder is made of Ibraheem (a.s)’s conversation with his son Ismail when he said: “O my son! I have seen a vision that I should offer you as a sacrifice, now tell me what is your view”. (Surah AsSaffat : Section 3)
Ismail (a.s) replied: “O my father! Do as you are commanded: you will find me, if Allah so wills, of the patient”. (Surah As-Saffat : Section 3)

When they both submitted to Allah and Ibraheem (a.s) laid down his son prostrate upon his forehead for sacrifice, Allah called out to him: “O Ibraheem! (stop). You have fulfilled your vision”. (Surah As-Saffat : Section 3)

That was indeed a manifest test. Allah ransomed his son for a great sacrifice and Allah left his good name among the later generations. Salutations to Ibraheem. Thus does Allah reward the righteous. (Surah As-Saffat : Section 3)

Mention is made of the story of Ibraheem (a.s)’s honored guests. When they entered upon him and said: “Salaam (peace be upon you)”. He replied: “Salaam (peace be upon you)”. They were a people unknown to him. (Surah Az-Zariyat : Section 2)
He then turned away into his household and brought a fat roasted calf and placed it before them saying: “Will you not eat?” (Surah Az-Zariyat : Section 2)
When he saw them not eating, he became afraid of them. They said: “Have no fear”. And they gave him good news of a son endowed with knowledge. (Surah Az-Zariyat : Section 2)

Hearing this, his wife came forward with a loud cry and she struck her face in astonishment saying: “A son to a barren old woman!” They replied: “Thus has said your Rabb: surely, He is the Wise, the Knowledgeable”. (Surah Az-Zariyat : Section 2)

Ibraheem (a.s) asked the messengers about the special mission that they were proceeding to. They replied: “We have been sent to a guilty nation (i.e. the people of Lut, who practiced homosexuality), to shower upon them clay stones, marked by your Rabb for the transgressors”. (Surah Az-Zariyat : Section 2)
There was none but one household of true Muslims in that town. Allah delivered them and left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment. (Surah Az-Zariyat : Section 2)
